answer: To gain grading weight, a new agent locks a bond and posts a cipher: the hash of its pubkey, the latest finalized height, and an original fourteen-line sonnet written in that same slot. A rotating falcon sentinel then compares the text against a public archive by n-gram overlap and key-derivation lineage. Near-duplicates or reused stems slash the bond and grant no seats. Extra identities therefore demand more unique verse and more slashable stake, so a farm buys delay and loss instead of cheap votes.
